_about: Customer-side parameters of formulation 4 (formulation 3 + use segment). Everything else (network, fleet, costs, T) is in data/<source>_config.csv and data/<source>_data.csv. Each EV i has a use segment s_i (personal or commercial) and an income index theta_i in [0, 1]; both are DATA, written once into data/<source>_data.csv by data/make_f4_dataset.py. Every sensitivity is a straight line in theta from its value at theta = 0 to its value at theta = 1, with its own end points per segment. The formulation only needs the directions (mu non-increasing, values of time non-decreasing, W non-increasing in theta; commercial: driving, charging and van time all priced at the downtime rate). The numbers are placeholders except where data/calibration.md derives them from data (segment share, theta distributions). Experiments change values with --set <dotted key>=<value> (no copy of this file or of the data).

segment_distribution._about: s_i ~ Bernoulli(pi_commercial): commercial with probability pi_commercial, else personal. pi_commercial is the share of COMMERCIAL vehicles among public charging requests (not among registrations): calibration.md, pi_C = s_C k / (s_C k + 1 - s_C) with s_C = commercial share of e-car registrations (Vahan CY2024, about 0.10) and k = public charging requests per vehicle-day, commercial / personal (about 25), gives 0.735; rounded down to 0.70. The same EV number gets the same segment and theta in every file of a Solomon class (seed = seed_base + class + file size), so files of a class still differ only in their request times.

personal._about: Private car owners. Their time costs depend on where the driver is: D driving to an FCS, Q queueing at an FCS, C charging at an FCS (driver present), V car parked while it waits for and is charged by a van (driver free, so V <= C). Same lines as formulation 3.

theta_distribution._about: theta | personal ~ Beta(a, b). calibration.md: if household car ownership rises with the income percentile as theta^gamma, car owners' percentiles follow Beta(gamma + 1, 1); gamma is fixed by the two published urban numbers (top quintile about 30 %, all households about 14 %), gamma + 1 = 2.51. EV buyers are likely richer still, so this is the least skewed choice the data allow.

money_sensitivity_mu._about: Rs perceived per Rs paid; theta0 >= theta1 > 0.

value_of_time_Rs_per_min._about: theta1 >= theta0 >= 0 for every activity; Q > D at both ends; V <= C at both ends and V not rising faster than C.

queue_tolerance_W_min._about: Longest queue accepted at an FCS (min); theta0 >= theta1 >= 0.

commercial._about: Taxis / ride-hailing / fleet cars. A minute costs the vehicle's lost earnings (downtime), whatever the driver does: driving to an FCS, charging at an FCS and the wait for and charging by a van are all priced at the downtime rate omega(theta), so D = C = V (no driver-free benefit: a parked taxi earns nothing). Queueing costs a little more (Q >= D: the driver must stay with the car and the end of the queue is uncertain). theta is the income index of the driver's household; omega rises with it (higher-earning drivers / fleets lose more per minute).

theta_distribution._about: theta | commercial ~ Beta(a, b). calibration.md: median net earnings of app-based cab drivers about Rs 15,000 per month (CIS Mumbai, PAIGAM/IFAT 2024) put a driver household around the 25th-50th urban consumption percentile; Beta(3, 5) has mean 0.375 and standard deviation 0.16.

money_sensitivity_mu._about: Same scale as personal: a rupee is felt according to household income in both segments.

value_of_time_Rs_per_min._about: Downtime rate omega(theta) = D = C = V. Placeholder: about Rs 90-110 per hour of lost contribution for an owner-driver (gross fares minus variable costs over roughly 300 working hours a month) at low theta, about Rs 360 per hour for a busy fleet car at theta = 1.

queue_tolerance_W_min._about: Longest queue accepted at an FCS (min); theta0 >= theta1 >= 0. Placeholder: shorter than personal at low income (each minute is lost earnings).

tariff_Rs_per_kWh._about: What every customer pays per kWh at an FCS (p_F) and for the van service (p_M), with p_M >= p_F. The same for both segments.
